# Sprint preparation

The planning session goes well only when the groundwork is done beforehand. Two days before the sprint starts I go through a checklist: the backlog is ordered, every story has acceptance criteria, dependencies on other teams are named, and the trickiest items have had a dry run with one engineer to expose the unknowns. The order of operations is the real art: the risky work comes first, the easy wins fill the gaps.

Interruptions are the enemy once the sprint is running. If a question has to be answered mid-sprint because it was not prepared, the team loses half a day. Preparation is about removing the reasons to stop. I print the checklist and tick it off in the room so that everyone sees what is ready.

Afterwards I keep the list as a template for the next planning.
